entities.name: Jean d'Outremeuse
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jean d'Outremeuse, also known as Jean des Preis, was a prolific chronicler, poet, and notary from the Prince-Bishopric of Liège, whose life culminated with his death on November 25, 1400. Operating at the intersection of history and romance in the late Medieval period, d'Outremeuse epitomized a prevailing trend in vernacular historiography that blended factual accounts with legendary narratives. His monumental work, the *Myreur des Hystoires*, a universal chronicle spanning from the creation of the world to 1399, stands as a testament to his ambition to weave local Liègeois identity into the grand tapestry of world history, frequently through highly imaginative and fabricated tales.

The core of d'Outremeuse's literary output consists of two major historical works and a scientific treatise. The *Myreur des Hystoires*, comprising six volumes, is a vast compendium that notably integrates Arthurian legends, Charlemagne narratives, and a highly embellished account of Liège's origins, claiming its foundation by the Trojans. This chronicle, while factually unreliable by modern standards, absorbed and transmitted a wealth of medieval lore, including the tale of the Four Sons of Aymon. His *Geste de Liège*, an epic poem, further solidified the mythical foundations of his homeland, while his lapidary, a treatise on precious stones, showcased a different facet of his scholarly interests.
